function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** is an official authorization or instruction given by a higher authority—such as a government, organization, or governing body—to carry out a specific task, policy, or set of responsibilities. In many contexts, a mandate can refer to:

| Context | Typical Meaning |
|---------|-----------------|
| **Government & Politics** | A directive from a legislative body or executive branch that requires certain actions (e.g., a health mandate requiring vaccinations). |
| **Business & Finance** | An instruction from a client or regulator that authorizes a firm to act on their behalf (e.g., a banking mandate allowing a company to manage its accounts). |
| **International Relations** | A formal assignment from an international organization (e.g., the UN) to a country or entity to perform a mission. |
| **Legal** | A binding order or requirement imposed by law or regulation. |

In short, a mandate is a formal, often legally binding, instruction that obligates the recipient to perform a particular duty or follow a set of rules.
